title: Trace Sampler Roadmap Scrapbook — weekly notes
content:
Purpose: free-form capture for the week — experiments, ad-hoc queries, decisions that matter for sampling economics and dashboards. Treat like a lab notebook + standup log; verbatim notes and half-baked hypotheses are expected.

---

Monday standup (quick bullets):
- Marco: finished microbenchmark for per-route adaptive sampler; results look promising for 75th/95th p99 cost delta.
- Lena: updated Dashboard 'Trace Health -> Sampler Impact' with new heatmap timebucket. Need to rename legend labels.
- Diego: running production shadow of 10% for prefix-based caching changes; seeing 4% reduction in average tokenization CPU.
- Aisha: prepping rollout plan and fallbacks for canary.

Notes from design huddle (deep dive):
- Goal this phase: reduce token-level tracing cost by 20% without losing signal for regression alerts.
- Constraint: preserve at least 90% incident-detection recall for our key customer workflows (API-chat, embeddings-batch).
- Proposal: two-tier sampler that combines route-level reservoir + adaptive priority based on recent error-rate delta and latency percentile drift.
- Quick sketch of algorithm: maintain sliding window (30m) per-route metrics; if p50/p95 drift > threshold, bump sample weight; otherwise decay weight with half-life 45m.
- Open question: how to treat long-tail routes with very low QPS (0.1 rps) — reservoir size vs. TTL? suggestion: fixed min-kept traces (n=5/day) + on-error override.

Data & experiments this week:
- Per-route baseline snapshot (2027-07-08 00:00Z):
  * total traces/day: 1.2M
  * top 10 routes account for 62% of traces
  * avg sample rate global: 12%
  * median trace span count: 7
- Microbench: per-request sampling decision cpu cost: ~3.2us on p3-like instance (hot path). Acceptable.
- Shadow run (adaptive sampler v0.3) at 10% traffic for 48h:
  * cost delta: -8% token-trace CPU (est), -6% storage (compressed spans).
  * detection recall for synthetic injected incidents: 92% (good)
  * false positive signal increased slightly on route /v1/re-rank (noisy clients) — hypothesis: weight bumping reacting to client-side bursts.

Dashboard action items (Lena):
- Add new metric 'sample-weight-by-route' to Sampler Impact dashboard (panel id: SIR-17). Need to add a log-scale option for routes with wide QPS range.
- Create an alert that fires when sampled-rate deviates > 30% from configured target for more than 15m. Link to playbook.
- Build an explainer modal for 'why my route is being sampled less' (customer-facing console idea) — wireframe in product backlog.

Runbook / rollback plan (Aisha):
- Canary config: 3-stage rollout (shadow 10% -> canary 50% small region -> global 100%). Each stage 24h.
- Immediate rollback condition: detection-recall drops below 88% for any of the three customer-critical workflows OR p99 latency regression > 10% sustained 30m.
- Quick revert: feature flag toggles in control plane (ff-sampler-v2). Manual override route-by-route.

Ad-hoc queries & snippets (for engineers):
- PromQL for sampled rate by route (rough):
  sum(rate(traces_sampled_total{env="prod"}[5m])) by (route) / sum(rate(traces_total{env="prod"}[5m])) by (route)
- SQL for top cost contributors (approx):
  SELECT route, SUM(ingest_bytes) as bytes, COUNT(*) as traces FROM trace_events WHERE ts >= now()-interval '7 days' GROUP BY route ORDER BY bytes DESC LIMIT 25;
- Quick grep to locate problematic spans: grep -nR "re-rank" /var/log/trace-indexer/2027-07-08*.log

Observations / weirdness (notes to self):
- Storage compaction job sometimes holds onto deleted spans -> investigate GC window. Might bias cost numbers. Filed ENGOBS-1499.
- One partner integration sends extremely deep traces (span count > 400) for batch embedding jobs; need guardrails (max-span-cutoff) + sample-by-span-depth heuristic.
- Time skew observed on a subset of trace ingesters (kube nodes in eu-west-3) causing out-of-order buckets; affects sliding-window metrics. Ops to follow up.

Decisions made this week:
- Keep adaptive weight half-life at 45m for next experiment. Rationale: balances responsiveness and noise smoothing. (Decision log: D-2027-07-09-1)
- Minimum kept traces per-route: 5/day for routes with avg qps < 0.2. (Decision log: D-2027-07-09-2)

Action items (owner [ETA]):
- Marco: land sampler v0.3 -> v0.4 changes (handle burst hysteresis, PR ready). ETA: 2027-07-13.
- Lena: dashboard updates + new alert panel (SIR-17, SIR-22). ETA: 2027-07-12.
- Diego: investigate compaction GC window and produce repro steps. File follow-up. ETA: 2027-07-11.
- Aisha: update canary runbook + coordinate with SRE to reserve capacity in eu-west-3. ETA: 2027-07-12.

Meeting notes: mid-week async check-in (Wed)
- Short sync: ran a quick A/B check (shadow vs control) on memory footprint. Memory +4% peaked on v0.3 due to per-route cache; we need mem bound guard and LRU eviction.
- Agreed to add memory pressure threshold to sampler config (max-reserved-memory 512MB per node).

Customer impact / outreach:
- Noting that some customers saw slight reduction in trace volume from the shadow run. CS outreach: short note to affected customers explaining this is an experiment, offering opt-out. Draft in customer-success: CS-PR-66 (linked).

Risks & unknowns:
- Long-tail route safety: does min-kept 5/day introduce bias for low-volume incident triggers? Need to simulate.
- Interaction with KV-cache-based prefix dedupe — could double-suppress traces for certain retry patterns. Test matrix needed.

Next week goals (high level):
- Complete canary QA checklist and start stage 1 (shadow -> internal region).
- Validate recall for production-like incidents using synthetic injections across routes.
- Dashboard polish: add cohort filtering and exportable CSV for cost-analyst team.

Random snippets / ideas (brain dump):
- Could we expose a per-route "trace budget" in console that teams can spend (chargeback) — link to optimize roadmap.
- Consider adding a lightweight p30 metric (quick health) to decide sampling bump instead of p95-only. Helps reduce noise from p95 spikes.

References: ENGOBS-1423 (sampler roadmap), ENGOBS-1499 (compaction GC), Confluence page (playbook), GH PR 278 (sampler code).

End of week note: roughly optimistic; small regressions found but rollback guardrails look good. Keep tempo: short cycles, verify recall early.

-- Aisha
